chunks: It is narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man has with me some clear silver dirhams. He meets me and says: Do I not have with you such-and-such, a thousand clear dirhams? So I say: Yes. Then he says: Convert them into dinars at this rate and record them for me with you. So what do you think about this?
He said: If you have precisely determined the rate for him on that day, then there is no harm in that.
He said: So I said: I did not weigh it out for him, nor did I carry out a hand-to-hand exchange with him; it was only speech between me and him.
So he said: Are not the dirhams from with you and the dinars from with you? I said: Yes. He said: There is no harm in that.

key_terms.أَثْبِتْهَا: record it as established debt in the new currency
key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمِ: silver dirhams serving as the original monetary amount owed
key_terms.السِّعْرِ: the exchange rate applied in the conversion
key_terms.حَوِّلْهَا: convert it from one currency form to another
key_terms.دَنَانِيرَ: gold dinars to which the debt is being converted
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no legal objection or harm in it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to convert a debt from dirhams into dinars at an agreed exchange rate in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a ruling on converting a debt recorded in dirhams into dinars based on the exchange rate of that day. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام permits it when the rate is properly determined and both currencies are already in the possession of the debtor, indicating the permissibility of such internal conversion in a financial obligation.
